newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Tourism body declares war on child prostitution.
newsitem.headline: Tourism body declares war on child prostitution.

text.p: Tourism leaders from 60 countries vowed on Thursday to combat child prostitution, which is flourishing in several major Asian destinations.

"Our message to the world is we are on an all-out war against this type of social problem," Philippine Tourism Secretary Mina Gabor told reporters at the start of the two-day meeting of tourism ministers.
The World Tourism Organisation is holding its meeting in Manila to discuss the darker side of tourism, such as drugs, prostitution and child abuse.
Gabor said members of the organisation vowed to open extradition talks as part of their campaign against paedophiles.

"We are finding things that other countries are doing which can be adopted by other countries. We will talk about extradition treaties so that if they (paedophiles) escape us, we can still continue to get hold of them by putting on them the full force of the law on the other side," she said.
The Philippines plans to hold extradition talks with Spain, Guam, Portugal, Romania and Japan on Friday.

Gabor said the Philippines was looking at adopting the Australian tourism federation's code of ethic which aims to screen out travel services to individuals or institutions looking for child prostitutes.
Gabor said the body was planning to tap the Internet to promote the campaign.
Tourism leaders said rapid growth in the tourist industry worldwide had spawned prostitution and sex tours.

"In the past 20 years, an increasing number of foreign tourists and paedophiles are travelling to Asia and other regions of the world to have sex with children," said Ron O'Grady, chairman of a Thai-based organisation against child prostitution, pornography and trafficking.
O'Grady said at least one million children under 16 years old worked as prostitutes. He said "sex tourists" went to countries where there were less risks of getting caught.
